title: A Turn Everyone Can See
bigQuestion: How do a whistle, a line and a written number help everyone take fair turns?

story.title: Half Freeze, Half Run
story.kicker: One sharp sound tells a whole field what to do.
paragraphs: It is field day. Sixteen children stand on the grass. Eight stand with their toes behind a white line. Eight wait on the side.
The teacher lifts a whistle. Tweet! The eight at the line dash forward. The eight on the side stay still. They know their turn comes next.
Nobody had to shout. Nobody had to argue. The line showed where to wait. The whistle showed when to go. Everyone could see and hear the same thing.
Grown-up sports use the same tools. A referee holds a whistle. A track has a starting line. A rule book says how many may play.
story.think: What tells you when it is your turn at school?

lessons.title: The Referee's Whistle
lessons.mainIdea: In soccer, the referee is the one person who starts and stops play.
reading: A soccer match has a *referee*. The rule book for soccer is the Laws of the Game. Law 5 says the referee starts and stops play.
The referee uses a *whistle*. Its sharp sound carries across a big field. Every player hears the same signal at once. Fans hear it too.

words.d: the official who is in charge of a soccer match
a small tool that makes a sharp sound to start or stop play

look.title: Law 5: The Referee
look.text: Each match is controlled by a referee. The referee has full authority to enforce the Laws of the Game. The referee can stop, pause or end a match.
look.cite: IFAB, Laws of the Game, Law 5 (The Referee)
look.prompt: Why is it helpful that only one person holds this power?

check.q: Who starts and stops a soccer match?
check.why: Law 5 of the Laws of the Game gives this job to the referee.

check.q: Why does a whistle help on a big field?
check.why: The whistle's sharp sound carries across a big field.

check.q: What is soccer's rule book called?
check.why: Soccer's rule book is the Laws of the Game.

lessons.title: Wait Behind the Line
lessons.mainIdea: Runners wait behind one starting line so every racer begins from the same place.
reading: A race begins at a starting *line*. Every runner waits behind it. That way no one starts closer to the finish.
Runners must wait for the start signal. Leaving too soon is a *false start*. Under World Athletics rules, a false start can remove a runner from the race.

words.d: a painted mark that shows where a race begins

look.title: Toes Behind the Paint
look.text: Look at eight pairs of shoes behind a white line. Seven pairs stay still. One shoe slides over the paint before the signal. The starter calls the runners back.
look.prompt: Why did the starter call everyone back?

check.q: What is a false start?
check.why: A false start is leaving before the signal.

check.q: Why does everyone wait behind one line?
choices: so no one starts closer to the finish
check.why: One line means every runner starts from the same place.

check.q: Whose rules say a false start can remove a runner?
check.why: World Athletics writes the rules for track races.

lessons.title: Eleven on a Soccer Side
lessons.mainIdea: The Laws of the Game let each soccer team have eleven players on the pitch.
reading: Law 3 of the Laws of the Game is about players. It says a team has up to eleven players on the pitch. One of the eleven is the *goalkeeper*.
Other players wait at the side. They are *substitutes*. A substitute may come on when the referee allows it. Then a player on the pitch comes off.

words.d: the player who guards a team's goal
players who wait at the side and may come on later

look.title: Players on the Field at Once
look.cite: IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 3 (The Players); NFHS Basketball Rules: five players per team on the court
look.prompt: How many more players does a soccer team have than a basketball team?

check.q: How many players may one soccer team have on the pitch?
check.why: Law 3 allows up to eleven players per team.

check.q: Who is one of the eleven?
check.why: The goalkeeper is one of the eleven players.

check.q: When may a substitute come on?
check.why: A substitute comes on when the referee allows it.

lessons.title: From Nine to Five
lessons.mainIdea: Basketball began with nine players a side, and later rules set five.
reading: Naismith's first class had eighteen students. So his first game used nine players on each *team*. That was in December 1891.
Nine players crowded the small gym. Within a few years, rule makers chose five a side. Today five players per team are on the *court*.

words.d: a group of players who play on the same side
the marked floor where basketball is played

look.title: The First Class
look.text: Naismith wrote that his class had eighteen men. He picked two captains. The captains chose sides, nine on each team, and the first game began.
look.cite: James Naismith, Basketball: Its Origin and Development (1941)
look.prompt: Why did the first game have nine on a side?

check.q: How many students were in Naismith's first class?
check.why: Eighteen students made two teams of nine.

check.q: How many basketball players per team are on the court today?
check.why: Today the rules put five players per team on the court.

check.q: Why did rule makers change from nine?
check.why: Nine a side crowded the gym, so later rules set five.

lessons.title: Naismith Posts His Rules
lessons.mainIdea: Naismith wrote thirteen rules and posted them so every player could read them.
reading: Before the first game, Naismith wrote his *rules*. There were thirteen. He pinned them on a board in the gym. Every player could read them.
In January 1892, the rules were printed. They appeared in the school paper, The Triangle. Soon other schools could play the same game.

words.d: written words that say what players may and may not do

look.title: A Paper on the Board
look.text: Look at a sheet of paper pinned to a gym wall. It is 1891. Thirteen short rules are written on it. Eighteen students crowd around to read it before they play.
look.prompt: Why did Naismith pin the rules where everyone could see them?

check.q: How many rules did Naismith first write?
check.why: Naismith wrote thirteen rules for the first game.

check.q: Where did Naismith pin his rules?
choices: on a board in the gym
check.why: He pinned them on a board in the gym.

check.q: Where were the rules printed in 1892?
check.why: The rules appeared in The Triangle in January 1892.

lessons.title: Fair Means the Same Rule
lessons.mainIdea: A game is fair when both sides use the same written rules.
reading: A *fair* game uses one set of rules for both sides. Both soccer teams follow the same Laws of the Game. Both have eleven players.
In 1886, four British football groups formed the *IFAB*. It still guards the Laws of the Game. So a match in Brazil uses the same laws as one in Chicago.

words.d: using the same rules for each side
the International Football Association Board, formed in 1886, which keeps the Laws of the Game

look.title: Two Teams, One Book
look.text: Look at two teams walking onto a pitch. One team is from Brazil. One is from Chicago. They speak different languages. They follow the same seventeen Laws of the Game.
look.prompt: How can two teams play together if they speak different languages?

check.q: What makes a game fair?
choices: both sides use the same rules
check.why: Fair means the same rules for each side.

check.q: When was the IFAB formed?
check.why: Four British football groups formed the IFAB in 1886.

check.q: What does the IFAB keep?
check.why: The IFAB guards the Laws of the Game.

lessons.title: Illinois Schools Share Rules
lessons.mainIdea: The Illinois High School Association, begun in 1900, runs state contests for Illinois schools.
reading: In 1900, Illinois schools formed the *Illinois High School Association*. People call it the IHSA. It helps schools across the state follow shared rules.
The IHSA runs state contests. The first boys wrestling state champions were crowned in 1937. Girls wrestling had its first state finals in 2022.

words.d: the group that runs state school sports in Illinois, begun in 1900; also called the IHSA

look.title: IHSA Years
look.prompt: How many years passed between boys wrestling and girls wrestling state finals?

check.q: When did the IHSA begin?
check.why: The Illinois High School Association began in 1900.

check.q: When were the first girls wrestling state finals?
check.why: IHSA girls wrestling held its first state finals in 2022.

check.q: What does the IHSA do?
choices: writes soccer's Laws of the Game
check.why: The IHSA runs state contests for Illinois schools.

review.why: A false start is leaving before the signal.
